verdicts.reason: A keeps the NEW badge as a readable tilted sticker, but it floats between the can and the logo instead of sitting on the product. The can crowds the top edge, the legal line is illegibly small and the missing-asset placeholder sits right against it. B uses the same centred structure with a larger headline, but it shrinks the NEW badge to a speck jammed into the bottom row next to the legal text and placeholder, and the headline nearly touches that row.

A groups the NEW badge with the can on the right and has a clear headline-then-CTA flow. However, the CTA is offset left of the centred headline, the logo is stranded at the far left, the headline crowds the top edge, and the tiny legal text is squeezed between the CTA and the placeholder. B (the same image as in pair 1) has a cleaner centred column, but its NEW badge is reduced to an illegible speck and its bottom row is cramped.

A reads left to right (logo and headline, then the can with its NEW badge, then the CTA) and keeps the badge at a usable size. But the logo is not aligned to the headline's edge, the headline is smaller, and the legal text is microscopic in the bottom-left corner next to the placeholder. B makes the same mistakes as before: the NEW badge is trivialised and the cramped bottom strip holds the legal text and the placeholder.
